name: Vedic civilisation
title: The story of the Vedic age

text: About 3,500 years ago, people in the north of India made sacred hymns and texts called the Vedas.
They learned them by heart and passed them on by word of mouth, with great care.
src: The Vedic period, or Vedic age (c. 1500–c. 500 BCE) / the northern Indian subcontinent when the Vedic literature, including the Vedas (c. 1500–900 BCE), was composed
liturgical texts, composed and orally transmitted with precision

text: At first they lived in groups led by chiefs, mostly herding cattle, which they also used like money.
Later, with iron axes and ploughs, they cleared forests and grew wheat, rice and barley.
src: organised into tribes rather than kingdoms and living mainly by herding / barter with cattle as a unit of value / the tribal chief (rajan)
After about 1000 BCE iron axes and ploughs made it possible to clear the forests of the Gangetic plains / growing wheat, rice and barley

text: Their main gods were Indra, Agni, the god of fire, and Soma.
They poured offerings into a sacred fire and prayed for rain, cattle, long life and heaven.
src: The main gods were Indra, Agni and Soma / offerings poured into the sacrificial fire, the god Agni
with offerings poured into the sacrificial fire / People prayed for rain, cattle, sons, long life and heaven

text: The oldest of the Vedas, the Rigveda, was made more than 3,000 years ago.
People also played music on flutes, lutes, harps, cymbals and drums.
src: c. 1400–1000 BCE: The Rigveda, the oldest layer of the Vedas, is composed
The flute (vana), lute (vina), harp, cymbals and drums were played

text: In time the people formed kingdoms, such as the Kuru kingdom.
People came to be split into four ranks, with priests and nobles at the top and labourers and slaves at the bottom.
src: later, with iron tools, it settled the western Ganges Plain and formed kingdoms such as the Kuru
four estates emerged: Brahmin priests and warrior nobility on top, free peasants and traders third, and slaves, labourers and artisans, many from pre-Aryan groups, fourth

text: About 2,500 years ago the Vedic age ended, as cities grew and new faiths such as Buddhism began.
But Vedic ideas lived on and became a main part of later Hinduism.
src: c. 600–500 BCE: The Mahajanapadas, the first true cities and the śramaṇa movements, among them Jainism and Buddhism, mark the end of the period
its tradition became a main part of later Hinduism
